free_tier.stated: On-demand GPU-hour list prices on a third-party index, collected 2026-11-02, cheapest zone for each card: H100 SXM 1x Zone 2 USD 2.19; A100 PCIe 80GB 1x Zone 5 USD 1.49; L40S 1x Zone 13 USD 0.97; RTX 4090 8x Zone 22 USD 0.44; L4 1x Zone 19 USD 1.04; A10 1x Zone 7 USD 1.42. Twenty GPU models in 80 configurations. Billing is On-Demand from a prepaid credit balance that is debited every minute.
free_tier.notes: The vendor documentation table, last updated about a year earlier, prints H100 2.48, A100 80G 1.65, L40s 1.10 and RTX4090 0.66 USD per hour and lists no L4.

chaining: An A10 with 30 vCPU and 200 GB of system RAM for USD 1.42 an hour is the most CPU-per-GPU shape, which is what a data pipeline that touches the accelerator intermittently wants: the 24 GB card is small enough for embedding and inference work, and the 200 GB of RAM is where the batch lives. The zone labels are the reason not to read this as one price, because the same card is printed at different rates per zone
limits_note: No quota is stated: the page publishes a per-GPU hourly rate, VRAM, vCPU count, RAM and a zone label. The page header also prints 'From / hour $0.17' without naming the card or zone, so the true floor is below the cheapest row that carries a specification and is unverified.

identity_cost.detail: An account created by email or OAuth (GitHub or Google). Instances run on a prepaid credit balance that is topped up by credit card, bank transfer, Cash App Pay, Google Pay or Link; at zero credit the instances are stopped and storage volumes are deleted. Whether a card or a minimum top-up is needed before the first instance is unverified: behind a sign-up.
